text:
katie: seeing intermittent packet loss between GPU nodes in us-west-2, started ~04:10 UTC. training jobs show RPC timeouts and some grpc streams reset. not all pods, seems bursty and small-frame related :confused:

oncall-bot: ALERT: net.loss.rate > 0.5% on overlay-tunnel-0 in us-west-2 (detected at 04:12 UTC)

mira: can you paste the nodes/pods and a quick tcpdump? any recent kernel or NIC firmware changes?

katie: node list: gpu-pool-a-12, gpu-pool-a-13, gpu-pool-b-01. pods affected: trainer-rt-7, trainer-rt-9. quick tcpdump from gpu-pool-a-12 (captured on overlay device):

```
13:04:11.123456 IP 10.2.5.9.44345 > 10.2.6.11.50210: Flags [P.], seq 1250:1376, ack 2201, win 1024, length 126
13:04:11.123489 IP 10.2.5.9 > 10.2.6.11: UDP, length 64
13:04:11.123490 IP 10.2.5.9 > 10.2.6.11: UDP, length 64
13:04:11.123500 IP 10.04.5.9 > 10.2.6.11: UDP, length 64
# repeated small UDP frames, occasional ICMP frag needed -> frag_needed
```

katie: tcpdump shows a couple ICMP fragment-needed messages and a burst of <128B UDP frames. MTU on host is 9000.

sebastian: could be GSO/GRO interactions on the encap device + offload mishandling. what are ethtool -k and MTU on the tun/geneve interface?

mira: on similar infra we saw small-packet jitter when NIC offloads were enabled and ESXi hosts did tso/gso weirdness when encapsulation changed packet sizes. If these are RDMA-capable Mellanox boxes, RDMA bypass can create different path for large flows but small control-plane frames hit kernel.

katie: output from nodes:

```
# on gpu-pool-a-12
$ cat /sys/class/net/tun0/mtu
9000
$ ethtool -k tun0 | grep -E "gso|gro|tso"
#gso: on
gro: on
tso: on
```

katie: NIC vendor ConnectX-6, firmware last updated 2024-11 (no kernel changes recently).

mira: quick mitigation -- try disabling GSO/GRO on the overlay interface on a canary node and re-run the small-packet job. commands: `ethtool -K tun0 gso off gro off tso off`

sebastian: also try iperf3 UDP with small packet size to reproduce: `iperf3 -c <peer> -u -b 100M -l 64` and run `tcpdump -n -s0 -w /tmp/cap.pcap host <peer>`

katie: running iperf now between a pair of affected nodes — initial run shows 0.6% loss with 64B payloads. when I disabled gso/gro on the overlay on gpu-pool-a-12 loss dropped to ~0.08% within 60s.

mira: can you try toggling `tx-checksumming` and `rx-checksumming`? `ethtool -K tun0 tx off rx off` sometimes helps when checksums are being offloaded incorrectly for encapsulated frames.

katie: tried tx off/rx off too, similar improvement. but this is a perf hit for large flows so not a long-term config.

sebastian: longer term options: upgrade NIC firmware drivers that fix encapsulation offload bugs, disable offloads only on overlay device via systemd unit, or move control-plane small-packet traffic to host network (hostPort) to avoid encapsulation. also consider lowering VXLAN/Geneve encapsulation offload defaults on CNI side.

mira: also file to collect: full pcap from both ends, `ss -tunap` during failures, `perf top` if CPU is spiking on encap processing, and `dmesg` for firmware messages. I'd like kernel + driver versions from affected nodes too.

katie: collecting caps now, attaching to ticket INF-8234. dmesg shows a few mlx5_core warnings (timestamped same minute) — copying to ticket.

sebastian: can we QoS-shape the small control frames out-of-band? maybe set DSCP for gRPC keepalives so they don't contend with bulk data. low-effort: schedule rolling maintenance to apply firmware/drivers and verify.

mira: agree, schedule a canary and then a batch. also check if dedicated RDMA flows coincide: any RDMA job start times around 04:10? RDMA may change NIC resource partitions. katie can you correlate job starts?

katie: yes, both trainer-rt-7 and 9 launched synchronously from orchestrator at 04:09. correlation looks strong.

oncall-bot: NOTE: mitigation applied on gpu-pool-a-12 (gso/gro/tso off on tun0) at 04:35 UTC. Monitor for 30m.

katie: after mitigation we've had ~15 mins with no resets on the affected streams. rolling to gpu-pool-a-13 next for canary.

mira: thanks. next steps: 1) collect full artifacts and upload to INF-8234, 2) run canary with offloads disabled on subset, 3) plan firmware/driver upgrades and vendor follow-up (Mellanox), 4) consider CNI change to avoid encapsulation for control plane.

sebastian: I'll own the vendor ticket and driver upgrade plan. katie please add exact pcap filenames and timestamps.

katie: done. attaching /tmp/cap-gpu12-04_10.pcap and /tmp/cap-gpu13-04_11.pcap. thanks :pray:

mira: great work team. likelihood high this is offload+encap interaction amplified by synchronous RDMA/bulk job starts. will keep monitoring and update INF-8234 with root cause once vendor confirms.
